title: As an AI-native user, I can point an agent at llms.txt or agent-oriented docs
As an AI-native user, I can run the product headlessly / in CI for automation
As an AI-native user, I can plug MCP servers into this product so it can use their tools
As an AI-native user, I can connect an agent via an official MCP server
As an AI-native user, I can use an official CLI
As an AI-native user, I can drive the product through a documented public API
As an AI-native user, I can issue scoped/least-privilege API credentials for an agent
As an AI-native user, I can build against official SDKs
As an AI-native user, I can subscribe to events via webhooks
As an AI-native user, I can get AI-generated insights and suggestions from my data inside the product
As an AI-native user, I can set up automations that run autonomously in the background
As an AI-native user, I can delegate tasks to a built-in AI assistant inside the product
As an AI-native user, I can operate the product with natural-language commands
As an AI-native user, I can explore an interactive API reference with runnable examples
As an AI-native user, I can download a machine-readable API spec (OpenAPI or equivalent)
As an AI-native user, I can test against a sandbox environment without touching production data
As an AI-native user, I can rely on versioned APIs with a documented deprecation policy
As an AI-native user, I can perform bulk operations across many items at once
As an AI-native user, I can define rules that trigger actions automatically on events
As an AI-native user, I can schedule recurring jobs or workflows
As an AI-native user, I can version, review, and roll back my automations
As an ops lead, customer and recipient onboarding is programmatic — documented KYC/KYB endpoints or flows that clear a counterparty for sending and receiving before money moves
As a founder, I can see who I'm actually contracting with — the licensed or registered entities behind the product and the jurisdictions they cover, published rather than buried
As an ops lead, the platform documents its sanctions screening, wallet risk checks, and travel-rule handling — compliance machinery named specifically, not waved at
As a developer, I never operate blockchain infrastructure — the platform abstracts nodes, gas, and chain mechanics behind a conventional REST API with client libraries in my language
As a developer, I can rehearse everything without real funds — a documented sandbox or testnet mode covering payments, payouts, and conversions with test values that behave deterministically
As a developer, money movement emits signed webhooks — payment confirmed, payout settled, conversion executed — so my system tracks state without polling chains or dashboards
As a developer, conversion is a first-class API — quotes and executed conversions between fiat and stablecoins (and between stablecoins) with documented rates, fees, and settlement times
As a developer, I can embed a fiat-to-stablecoin onramp — a documented widget or API where end users buy stablecoins with cards or bank transfers inside my product
As an AI-native user, I can do everything through the API that I can do in the UI
As an AI-native user, I can export all of my data in open formats and leave
As an AI-native user, I can read the product's source under an open license
As an AI-native user, I can self-host the core product
As an ops lead, I can run mass disbursements — batch or bulk payout APIs that push many stablecoin or fiat payouts in one documented operation with per-item status
As an ops lead, recipients can land in local fiat — documented off-ramp rails that convert stablecoins into bank transfers across a published set of currencies and countries
As a developer, I can send stablecoin payouts programmatically — pay a wallet address or stored recipient through the API with documented status tracking to final settlement
As an AI-native user, I can choose where my data is stored (region/residency)
As an AI-native user, I can prevent my data from being used to train AI models
As an AI-native user, I can control data retention and deletion
As an AI-native user, I can opt out of telemetry and usage tracking
As a finance lead, settlement is legible — documented timing from payment to available balance, published fees per rail, and statements or reports my accounting can consume
As a finance lead, I can move value between fiat and stablecoin balances on the platform — internal transfers and rebalancing through the API or dashboard, documented end to end

As a developer, I can accept a stablecoin payment from a customer through a documented checkout or payment API — create the payment, present the address or flow, and confirm settlement programmatically
As a developer, the platform documents which stablecoins and chains it supports — USDC, USDT and peers across multiple named networks — so I can match what my customers actually hold
As a finance lead, I can take crypto payments but settle in fiat — a documented option to auto-convert stablecoin receipts into a fiat balance or bank payout so my books never hold crypto
As an AI-native user, an agent can move stablecoins under scoped authority — documented agent payment flows where an agent initiates a payment or payout with spend controls a human configured
As an AI-native user, agents can hold and use wallets safely — programmatic wallet issuance for agents with scoped keys, policy controls, and documented limits on what an agent can move
As an AI-native user, the platform speaks the machine-payment protocols by name — x402, ACP, MPP, or AP2 support documented with endpoints or SDKs, not just a blog aspiration
As a founder, I can issue a branded stablecoin on the platform's infrastructure — a documented issuance product covering minting, redemption, and reserve management, with its gating quoted honestly
As a finance lead, the economics of held stablecoins are documented — reserve composition, attestations, and any yield or rewards program with its eligibility and regulatory caveats stated plainly
As a finance lead, my business can hold a stablecoin balance on the platform — documented custodial accounts with stated availability, geographies, and any gating quoted honestly
As a developer, incoming funds are attributable — named virtual accounts or dedicated deposit addresses per customer so reconciliation knows who paid without manual matching
As a developer, I can create wallets programmatically — per-customer or per-purpose wallets and deposit addresses provisioned through the API with documented key custody semantics
